If you want a pricier card you can go with Nvidia GTX 1070 or 1080. However they really are pricier. Probably the best thing would be to do your own research and find the solution best for you.

Probably best to wait for aftermarket 480s. Graphics cards usually exceed PCIe specs for power consumption. But I think AMD's big mistake is that this card is ending up in a lot of old, mid and low end motherboards that can't cope as well. Motherboards have an alarmingly high rate of starting on fire, check out youtube. It's not something new, but it's definitely something scary.

There's sort of a paradox, I wouldn't put a reference 480 in a budget motherboard, but 480 is a budget card. I really wish AMD went with an 8-pin though, it would have left a lot of room for overclocking and it would have helped a ton. The reference cards aren't overclocking very well either. I think it has to do with the power delivery and the cooling. Which is a shame, because there's rumors of them breaking 1500mhz, but not on a reference design.

I wouldn't waste money on a 480 at all if your goal is VR. The 1060s are due out this fall and they'll be cheaper than the 1070 and and perform much better than the 480. General MSRP estimates (based on the 960, no confirmed pricing yet) place the price at between $179 and $229.
